paragraphs: Meporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar taame hammitzot parashat eqeb tekavven behemshek zeman akilateka, ulepachot kesheatta okel otah happerusa shel kazzayit asher birkat aleha hammotzi kavvana qetzara derek kelal vezo hi ki hinneh inyan habberur hu "y l"b shinnayim shehem keneged l"b netibot chakema hammebarerin hakkol dibmachashaba etbarer kolla, vehem hattochanin umeporarin et hammaakol veal yede ken mitbarer haokel mittok happesolet kederek harechayim hattochanot et hattebua veaach"k mittaperin hassubbin vehammursan shehem haqqelippot min haqqemach shehu haokel, mah sheen ken qodem shennitchan shehayu debeqim yachad betaklit ad kan leshono veod katub sham lekavven bishte bechinot shel berur bemaakol sheokel, vehu haechad hu berur hammaakol beatzmo hattob shebbo min hassigim hamorabim bo "y chete adam harishon, vegam od mah shehaya meorab bahem mittechillat beriyyatan mishsheshet yeme bereshit, vehashsheni hu inyan tiqqun nepashot hamgulgalim hannimtzaot bemaakol umashqeh ayyen sham, od katub sham vezeh leshono: tekavven libloa hammaakol achar shennitchan ki sham baistomeka hu gemar habberur, ki az mitakkel hammaakol vehattob shebbo mithappek ledam, vehammazon holek el hakkabed umitpashshet bekol haoreqim vehaebarim kannoda, vehara shebbo yored derek bene meayim veyotze lachutz ad kan leshono vekol ellu kavvanot peshutot hen utzerikot meod apillu leadam pashut, vetzarik shekkol adam yodea seper lehargil atzmo bahem vbsh"q mqbtzyl katabti "g derabbenu za"l katab dehabberur tzarik lihyot "y l"b shinnayim shehem keneged netibot chakema venishna dabar zeh paamayim shalosh bidbarayv beshaar taame hammitzot, im kol zeh im yimmatze adam shennapelu shinnayv velo nishar lo ki im arba o shesh al tachshob dechassore michassera zeh min tiqqun hannizkar, ella apillu bazeh hammeat hannishar oseh hattiqqun meshallem meachar demittechilla hayu lo l"b shinnayim vezeh hannishar mechila dl"b netibot chakema qaate, vedugma lazeh timtza bedin netilat yadayim dimtaharin hammayim deshiyyure tahora mishshum deatu mishshiur shalem vekannizkar beshulchan aruk siman q"s seip y"g, deyesh mattirim apillu benotelin zeh achar zeh veku' manni shebbau mishshiyyure tahora yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: The Ari wrote that one should have the intention of extraction (birur) at the time of eating: the extraction is accomplished through the thirty-two teeth, which correspond to the thirty-two Paths of Wisdom, which grind and separate the food from the waste like millstones separating bran from flour. One should have intention regarding two extractions: the extraction of the food itself from the dross mixed into it from the sin of Adam HaRishon and from the six days of Creation, and the rectification of reincarnated souls found in food and drink. Upon swallowing, when the food reaches the stomach, the extraction is completed: the good turns into blood and nourishes the body, and the bad exits through the intestines. These intentions are simple, and every literate person should accustom himself to them, or at least have this intention with the piece of HaMotzi. And one whose teeth have fallen out and few remain should not think the rectification is lacking, since even the small remainder — coming as it does from the power of the thirty-two Paths — accomplishes the rectification in full.
takeaways: At the time of eating, one has intention of extracting the good from the waste (thirty-two teeth corresponding to the thirty-two Paths)
Even one with few remaining teeth accomplishes the rectification in full

paragraphs: Otam shiyyure maakol hannissaim baatzamot ubaqqelippin shel happerot im yesh bahem netzutze qedushsha yitbareru "y beraka acharona sheomer haadam al shulchano "p shessopam lezarqam laashpa, lepikak yizzaher haadam shello yasir meal hashshulchan atzamot uqelippin ella ad leachar birkat hammazon kemo shekkatebu hamqubbalim veken katab bechesed laalapim siman q"p ot ', ulekak azhara shamanu shello yotzi meal hashshulchan dabar lehaakil libhema vechayya veop hattemeim qodem birkat hammazon vekannizkar sham, veotam bene adam sheddarkan leekol tabshilin shel basar maaseh qedera techilla veachar akilatam yabiu perot al hashshulchan, veellu qasheh lahem lehannicha kelim shel happerot bihyoto hashshulchan mepuzzar alayv atzamot shel basar vekayyotze, hinneh yesh ledabar zeh taqqana sheyyepareshu al hashshulchan mappa acheret kede sheyyitkassu haatzamot velikluke hattabshilin visadderu al mappa hanneqiyya kelim shel perot sheyyabo, venimtza aach"k mebarekim birkat hammazon bihyot haatzamot vehaqqelippin odam al hashshulchan ubazeh yushlam beruram:

clarification.explanation: Leftover bits of food remaining on bones and on fruit peels — if they contain sparks of holiness, they are extracted through the final berachah a person recites at his table, even though they will ultimately be thrown into the trash. Therefore one should be careful not to remove bones and peels from the table except after Birkat HaMazon (as the Kabbalists wrote, and Chesed LaAlafim). For this reason, one also should not take anything from the table to feed to non-kosher domestic animals, beasts, or fowl before Birkat HaMazon. And those whose custom is to eat meat dishes first and then bring fruit, who find it difficult to place the fruit dishes on a table scattered with bones and mess — there is a remedy for this: spread another tablecloth over the table to cover the bones and remains of the cooked dishes, and arrange the fruit dishes on the clean tablecloth; thus they recite Birkat HaMazon while the bones and peels are still on the table, and their extraction is thereby completed.
takeaways: Bones and peels are not removed from the table until after Birkat HaMazon — the berachah extracts the sparks of holiness within them.
One likewise should not take food from the table to feed non-kosher animals or fowl before Birkat HaMazon.
If the table is messy, spread a clean tablecloth over it and arrange the fruit on top, leaving the bones underneath until Birkat HaMazon.

paragraphs: Meachar shebbirkat hammazon oseh tiqqun gadol al hashshulchan vekaamur, lekak hizhiru chaza"l leshayyer haadam pat al shulchano beet birkat hammazon, ubazzohar haqqadosh hechmiru bazeh veasmekuha aqqera d"l tissa et shem Adonai eloheka lashshave" (shemot k, z), veim akelu kol happat qodem birkat hammazon velo hirgishu ella ad sheat birkat hammazon lo yabiu pat shelema veyannichu al haheshlachan ella yabiu perusa, veim haya al hashshulchan pat shelema meet shebberak hammotzi lo yesirenna bishat birkat hammazon veadderabba adip tepe lemebad haki lehashir kikkar echad shalem al hashshulchan meet shebberek hammotzi, velo aseru bepat shelema ella raq im yebienna mechadash beet habbirkat hammazon:

clarification.explanation: Since Birkat HaMazon effects a great rectification upon the table, our Sages warned to leave bread on the table during the berachah, and the Zohar treated this stringently, basing it on the verse "You shall not take the Name of the Lord your God in vain." If they ate all the bread and did not notice until the time of the berachah, they should not bring a whole loaf but rather a slice. And if there was a whole loaf on the table from the time of HaMotzi, one should not remove it — indeed it is preferable to leave a whole loaf there from the time of HaMotzi; a whole loaf was only prohibited when brought anew at the time of Birkat HaMazon.
takeaways: Bread is left on the table during Birkat HaMazon
If all was eaten, bring a slice; but a whole loaf that was already there from the start is not removed

paragraphs: Tzarik lizzaher shello yishshaer keli req al hashshulchan bishat birkat hammazon, kegon kappot kosot uqearot vekayyotze, gam yizzaher shello lehannicha sakkin al hashshulchan beet birkat hammazon:

clarification.explanation: One must be careful that no empty vessel remain on the table at the time of Birkat HaMazon, such as spoons, cups, and bowls, and one must likewise be careful not to leave a knife on the table during the berachah.
takeaways: No empty vessel is left on the table during Birkat HaMazon
No knife is left on the table during the berachah

paragraphs: Asur leabbed perurin sheyyesh bahem kezayit, lekak yizzaher shello yippelu tippot mayim min netilat yadayim al perurin shebbashshulchan ki yimmaasu bekak, vaapillu en bahem kazzayit asur leabbedam ulehamisam deqasheh laaniyyut bar minan apillu bedabar muat, veazhara zo tzerika yoter lenashim shehem metzuyim babbayit veenehem tihyena meshotetot tamid beqarqa habbayit baabur zot veeshet chayil tekabbed beyadeha tamid meqom haakila achar haakila vetizroq lattannur, veal tismok al hamsharet veaz aleha neemar (mishle l, y): "batach bah leb balah veshalal lo yechsar", velazeh ameru (baba metzia kt.): en habberaka metzuya bebeto shel adam ella baabur ishto, yaan ki tashgicha shello leabbed perurin qetannim, veaz baalah shalal lo yechsar ki lo yechsar lachmo, veyizzaharu lenappetz hammappa shel hashshulchan betannur, ubelel shabbat yinnatzu otah bemaqom meyuchad lazeh, veachar shabbat yekabbedu maqom asher nippetzo bo veyizrequ lattannur, veken tizzaher haishsha lekabbed maqom shemmatzniin bo hallechem ulekabbedo velizroq lattannur, ki mukrach sheyyihyeh sham perurin beet haknasa vehotzaa, veken yizzaharu mokere hallechem bashshuq lekabbed sebibot haqquppa shemmokerin bah hallechem ki yippelu perurin harbeh keshemmotziin hallechem mimmenna lishqol lalloqechim, veyizrequ heapar im happerurin shebbo lattannur, veazhara zo tzerika yoter poh ayarenu shehallechem hu qal veeno ab kol kak yaan deeno maaseh pvry"n (tannur apiyya baal mishshetach meozen, upiv min hatztzad) (bearbe tzamun (kikkar lechem agulla vetappucha)) veal ken yippol mimmennu perurin harbeh yoter millechem maapeh hpvr"n, lekak tzarik lehazhir hamon haam bazeh, ubiprat birqiqin dei epshar shello yippol mehem perurin:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to waste crumbs containing a kezayit, and therefore one should be careful that water drops from netilat yadayim not fall on the crumbs on the table and make them repulsive. And even crumbs that do not contain a kezayit, it is forbidden to waste and make them repulsive, for this brings hardship of poverty even over a small matter. This warning applies especially to women who are found in the home, and a woman of valor should always sweep the eating area with her own hands and throw the crumbs into the oven, and not rely on the servant; of her it is said, "Her husband's heart trusts in her, and he shall lack no gain." One should shake out the tablecloth into the oven (on Shabbat night, in a designated place, and afterward sweep and throw into the oven), and sweep the place where the bread is stored. Likewise bread sellers in the market should sweep around the place of sale and throw the crumbs into the oven. This warning is especially needed where the bread is light and soft and sheds many crumbs, and particularly with wafers.
takeaways: It is forbidden to waste crumbs, and certainly a kezayit; one should not let handwashing water drip onto them
Women and bread sellers should be careful to sweep the eating area and bread storage/sale area and throw the crumbs into the oven

paragraphs: Qodem birkat hammazon yizzaher littol mayim acharonim letok hakkeli ki mayim acharonim choba apillu akal pat bilbad deyesh bah taam gadol "p hazzohar haqqadosh vedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar taame hammitzot parashat eqeb, vekatub sham beet netilat mayim acharonim yechabber arba haetzbaot lebad vehaggudal lebad veyashpil etzbeotayv kelappe matta:

clarification.explanation: Before Birkat HaMazon one should be careful to take mayim acharonim into a vessel, since mayim acharonim is obligatory even if one ate only bread, and it has a great reason according to the Zohar and the Ari. At the time of taking it, one should join the four fingers together separately and the thumb separately, and lower the fingers downward.
takeaways: Mayim acharonim is obligatory even when one ate only bread, taken into a vessel
Join the four fingers together and the thumb separately, fingers pointed downward

paragraphs: Bemaamar rabbotenu za"l hannizkar sheameru: mayim acharonim choba, ramuz kamma kavvanot sodiyyot shel mayim acharonim, velaken tob shehaadam qodem sheyyoshit yado littol mayim acharonim yomar halaka zo mayim acharonim choba, veshamati meateret rashe harab mor abi za"l shehaya minhag ateret rashe harab mv"r zeqeni rabbenu mosheh chayyim za"l lomar halaka zo qodem netilat mayim acharonim, velipamim haya samuk al halaka zo bimqom dibre tora sheomerim al hashshulchan qodem birkat hammazon kesheen shehut lomar dibre tora, ki zo halaka mittora shebbeal peh, vedabar beitto mah tob:

clarification.explanation: In the Sages' statement "mayim acharonim is obligatory" several secret intentions are hinted, and therefore it is good that before extending one's hand to take mayim acharonim, one should say this halachah, "mayim acharonim is obligatory." This was likewise the custom of Rabbeinu's grandfather, and at times he relied on saying this halachah in place of words of Torah said at the table before Birkat HaMazon when there was no time, since this is a halachah of the Oral Torah.
takeaways: It is good to say "mayim acharonim is obligatory" before taking it, since intentions are hinted within it
This halachah can serve as words of Torah at the table when there is no time

paragraphs: Yizzaher sheyyihyu mayim haacharonim meat velo yarbeh bahem ki hemma cheleq hassitra achara, veim yadayv mezohamot harbeh min hattabshil veken piv usepamo shetztzarik lahem mayim harbeh birchitzatam, tob sheyyirchatzem qodem netilat mayim acharonim addata leekol od aach"k, veyihyu ellu kemayim emtzaim veken yaaseh, achar sheyyirchatzem yokal chatikat pat min hashshulchan kede shello tihyeh nechshebet rechitza hahi lemayim acharonim, veachar sheyyokal chatikat happat vekayyotze yittol mayim acharonim meat vibarek birkat hammazon veayyen kap hachayyim siman k"h ot b':

clarification.explanation: One should be careful that the mayim acharonim be little and not use much of it, since it is the portion of the Sitra Achra. And if one's hands are very soiled from the cooked dish, and likewise the mouth and mustache requiring much water, it is good to wash them beforehand with the intention of continuing to eat, and these count as "intermediate water"; after washing, one should eat a piece of bread so that this washing not be counted as mayim acharonim, and then take a small amount of mayim acharonim and recite the berachah.
takeaways: Mayim acharonim should be little, as it is the portion of the Sitra Achra
For very soiled hands: wash first as "intermediate water," eat bread, then take a small amount of mayim acharonim

paragraphs: Katebu haacharonim beshem hamqubbalim za"l keshennotel mayim acharonim yomar "zeh cheleq adam rasha meelohim" (iyyob k, kt), vikavven chalaq adam rasha rashe tebot "achar" dehu hassitra achara veayyen kap hachayyim, vekatabti bsh"q mqbtzyl dehannoheg bazeh yomar debarim ellu belachash, vehammaskil yabin:

clarification.explanation: The later authorities wrote in the name of the Kabbalists that when taking mayim acharonim one should say, "This is the portion of a wicked man from God," with the intention that "chelek adam rasha" is an acrostic for "achar" (the Sitra Achra). One who follows this practice should say these words in a whisper.
takeaways: It is customary to say "This is the portion of a wicked man from God" during mayim acharonim
And to say it in a whisper

paragraphs: En notelin mayim acharonim "g qarqa ella bikli, veim i epshar limtzo keli yittol "g etzim o al haritzpa deen rucha raa shora al haritzpa kemo sheshshora "g qarqa, vegam mayim emtzaiyyim shennotelin ben chalab lebasar g"k tzerikin keli:

clarification.explanation: One does not take mayim acharonim onto the ground but into a vessel. If no vessel can be found, one should take it onto wood or onto the floor, since no evil spirit rests upon a floor as it does upon bare ground. And mayim emtza'im, taken between eating dairy and meat, likewise requires a vessel.
takeaways: Mayim acharonim into a vessel; if none available, onto wood or floor, not bare ground
Mayim emtza'im (between dairy and meat) likewise requires a vessel

paragraphs: En notelin bechammin shehayyad nikvet bahem, veyesh omerim tzarik sheyyihyu tzonenin mammash venakon lehizzaher bazeh, veyesh mi sheomer shetztzarik sheyyihyu reuyim lishtiyya shello yihyu marim o seruchim, gam tzarik sheyyihyu baim mikkoach gabra, veim abar velo natal mayim acharonim yittol achar birkat hammazon, veim en lo mayim yittol bishar mashqin vaapillu beyayin kevan deen lo littol beinyan acher:

clarification.explanation: One does not take mayim acharonim with water hot enough to scald the hand, and some say it must be actually cold, and it is proper to be careful about this. Some say it must be fit for drinking — not bitter or foul-smelling — and must come by human effort. If one forgot and did not take mayim acharonim, he should take it after Birkat HaMazon; and if he has no water, he may use another beverage, even wine, since he has no other way.
takeaways: The water should not be too hot, and it is proper that it be cold and fit for drinking
If one forgot: take it after the berachah; if no water is available, use another beverage

paragraphs: Tzarik littol ad pereq shel haetzbaot kak katebu happesuqim za"l, venireh li shetztzarik littol ad pereq hashshelishi verosh pereq hashshelishi biklal, deken nireh milleshon rabbenu harasha"sh za"l besiddur shekkatab vekavvin bintilat y"d pirqe yamin veku' yeuyyan sham, mashma dehannetila hi ly"d peraqim vehaki mistabbera:

clarification.explanation: One must take mayim acharonim up to the joint of the fingers. In Rabbeinu's view, one must take up to and including the third joint, since it appears from the wording of the HaRash"ash in his siddur, who wrote to have intention in the taking regarding the fourteen joints of the hand, implying that the taking covers all fourteen joints.
takeaways: Mayim acharonim is taken up to the joint of the fingers
In Rabbeinu's view, up to and including the third joint (fourteen joints)

paragraphs: Hammoded melach vehannogea bemelach chayyab littol yadayv aach"k, veken apillu belo seuda kesheokel qishshuin vekayyotze bidbarim sheddarkan lehannicha alehem melach beetzbeotayv tzarik littol yadayv aach"k, d"g demelach sedomit eno matzuy yesh lachush lemin melach shettibo kemelach sedomit vekol adam yachush leatzmo leqayyem dibre chakamim veayyen chesed laalapim ushear acharonim:

clarification.explanation: One who measures salt or touches salt must wash his hands afterward. Likewise, even without a formal meal, when eating cucumbers and similar things that people typically salt with their fingers, one must wash his hands afterward, since although Sodomite salt is not commonly found, one should be concerned about a type of salt whose nature resembles it (which blinds the eyes), and every person should be concerned for himself to fulfill the words of the Sages.
takeaways: One who touches salt washes his hands afterward, out of concern for salt resembling Sodomite salt
This applies even outside a meal, when touching salt with one's fingers

paragraphs: Yesh mi sheomer im akal maakol lach sheaz yadayv mezohamot bo, az min haddin kesheyyirchatz yadayv mebarek al rechitzat yadayim, veal nahagu haolam lebarek ken "g dehammatzrikin beraka zo hem gedole olam, deqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel, mihu tzarik kol adam leharher beraka zo belibbo:

clarification.explanation: There is an opinion that if one ate a moist food that soiled his hands, then by strict law he should recite "al netilat yadayim" when washing his hands afterward. But the common practice is not to recite this berachah, even though the great authorities who require it are significant, since we hold that in cases of doubt regarding berachot we are lenient; nevertheless, every person should have this berachah in mind in his heart.
takeaways: Some hold one should recite "al netilat yadayim" after a moist food, but common practice does not, since doubtful berachot are treated leniently
One should have the berachah in mind in his heart

paragraphs: Tzarik lehizzaher shello lehapsiq ben mayim acharonim lebirkat hammazon apillu bedibre tora, veraq pesuqim ellu yomar otam achar mayim haacharonim qodem birkat hammazon vehem hammizmor elohim yechannenu vibarekennu kullo vetob letzayyer bemachshabto betzurat hammenora, veacharayv yomar abaraka et Adonai bekol et vego' vikavven legaresh hassitra achara haomedet al hashshulchan, veacharayv pasuq sop dabar hakkol nishma vego', upasuq tehillat Adonai yedabber pi vego' upasuq vaanachnu nebarek yah meatta vead olam halluyah, veaach"k vaydabber elay zeh hashshulchan asher lipne Adonai, vikavven sope tebot zeh al hashshulchan asher nh"r, vibarek birkat hammazon beenayim segurot kitpillat haamida, veyasim yad semol keneged hechazeh veyad yamin al yad semol vibarek bekavvana, dehassitra achara omed sham leqatreg alayv im lo yebarek bekavvana:

clarification.explanation: One must be careful not to interrupt between mayim acharonim and Birkat HaMazon, even with words of Torah. One should say only these verses after mayim acharonim, before the berachah: the entire psalm "Elohim Yechoneinu Vivarcheinu" (and it is good to visualize the shape of the Menorah in one's mind), "Avarechah et Hashem bechol et" (with the intention of driving away the Sitra Achra standing at the table), "Sof davar hakol nishma," "Tehillat Hashem yedaber pi," "Va'anachnu nevarech Kah me'atah ve'ad olam, Halleluyah," and "Vayedaber elai: zeh hashulchan asher lifnei Hashem" — with intention on the final letters of this verse (zeh-hashulchan-asher), which allude to the word "NaHaR," as a further secret in the intention of the berachah. He should recite Birkat HaMazon with eyes closed as in the Amidah, left hand against the chest and right hand upon it, with intention, since the Sitra Achra stands ready to accuse if he does not bless with intention.
takeaways: One does not interrupt between mayim acharonim and the berachah, but does recite special verses
In the final verse (Vayedaber elai zeh hashulchan) one also has intention on the final letters, which allude to the secret of "NaHaR"
One recites the berachah with eyes closed and with intention, right hand upon the left against the chest

paragraphs: Yishtaddel lebarek al hakkos im yesh shenayim immo sheaz yesh lahem zimmun, abal yechidi lo yebarek al hakkos, vetzarik sheyyimsor lo hakkos adam acher kesheochazo bishte yadayv, veken hu yeqabbelennu bishte yadayv, veqodem sheyyomar vaydabber elay zeh hashshulchan vego' az yeqabbel hakkos bishte yadayv, veachar sheyyeqabbel oto bishte yadayv yeechoz oto beyad yamin bilbad, veaz yomar vaydabber elay zeh hashshulchan vego' veyatchil laasot zimmun ulebarek:

clarification.explanation: One should strive to recite the berachah over a cup when there are two others with him (forming a zimmun), but one alone should not recite the berachah over a cup. Another person should hand him the cup while holding it with both hands, and the one reciting the berachah should receive it with both hands. Before saying "Vayedaber elai: zeh hashulchan" he should receive the cup with both hands, and afterward hold it with the right hand alone, and then say "Vayedaber elai: zeh hashulchan" and begin the zimmun and the berachah.
takeaways: The berachah over a cup is recited with a zimmun (three), not alone
One receives the cup with both hands, and after saying "Vayedaber elai" holds it with the right hand alone

paragraphs: Minhag hachasidim keshemmebarekin birkat hammazon al hakkos sheyyihyeh happat shebbashshulchan munnach letzad semol hambarek, kede sheyyihyeh kos shel beraka beyamin shello vehappat bismolo, veyesh taam baddabar al derek hassod:

clarification.explanation: The custom of the pious ones is that when reciting Birkat HaMazon over a cup, the bread on the table is placed to the left of the one reciting the berachah, so that the cup of blessing is in his right hand and the bread in his left, and there is a reason for this in the way of the mystical tradition.
takeaways: The bread is placed to the left of the one reciting the berachah, and the cup in his right hand
There is a mystical reason for this

paragraphs: Kos birkat hammazon tzarik haddacha mibbipnim ushetipa mibbachutz, gam tzarik sheyyihyeh chay, veyesh bazeh kamma deot deyesh omerim hakkavvana hu debitchillat habberaka lo yihyeh mazug shello yimzegennu ella ad birkat haaretz veyesh omerim dehakkavvana hu sheyyemalleennu min hatztzelochit o mehechabit leshem beraka velo yihyeh mishshiyyure kosot, veyesh omerim hakkavvana sheyyihyeh hakkos shalem, umin haddin tzarik lehizzaher bekol hassebarot hannizkarot leqayyem otam. veachar sheyyimzegennu bebirkat haaretz yihyeh male, ak lo yehi hammale kol kak sheyyihyeh nishpak mimmennu, veachar sheyyeqabbelennu bishte yadayv mishte yadayim shel hannoten yishshaer beyad yamin bilbad bekol habberaka kullah, velo tesayyea hassemol leyamin, gam tzarik sheyyagbihennu min hashshulchan tepach lepachot, venoten enayv bo bekol habberaka shello yassicha dato mimmennu, veachar sheyyishtehu yeshayyer meat yayin bo leshaggero leishto apillu lo akela immo:

clarification.explanation: The cup of Birkat HaMazon requires rinsing on the inside and washing on the outside, and must be "chai" (undiluted wine). There are differing views on the meaning of "chai": some say it should not be mixed with water at the start of the berachah, only mixed in at Birkat Ha'aretz; some say it should be filled from the flask or barrel for the sake of the berachah and not from leftover cups; and some say the cup itself should be whole and undamaged. By strict law one should be careful regarding all these views. After mixing it in at Birkat Ha'aretz it should be full (but not so full that it spills), and after receiving it with both hands it should remain in the right hand alone throughout the berachah (the left should not assist), raised a handbreadth from the table, with his eyes on it throughout the berachah so his mind not wander; and after drinking, he should leave a little wine to send to his wife, even if she did not eat with him.
takeaways: The cup requires rinsing, washing, and to be "chai" (per the views: mixed only at Birkat Ha'aretz, filled fresh, whole)
Held in the right hand, raised a handbreadth, eyes kept on it, and wine left over for one's wife

paragraphs: Itter yad katebu happoseqim yittelennu bimino shehu semol kol adam, venireh li bs"d "p hassod gam itter yad yittelennu beyamin deen taluy bayyad kaka , veayyen shalme tzibbur dap m' halaka y"d beshem mahari"y tzemach za"l gabbe tepillin yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: The halachic authorities wrote that a left-handed person should take the cup in his own right hand (which is the left hand of most people). But in Rabbeinu's view, based on the mystical tradition, even a left-handed person should take it in the right hand (the right hand of most people), since the matter does not depend specifically on this hand.
takeaways: The halachic authorities: a left-handed person takes the cup in his own right hand
Rabbeinu, based on the mystical tradition: even a left-handed person takes it in the usual right hand

paragraphs: Tzarik shello yihyeh pagum sheim shata mimmennu pegamo, vaapillu shata min hakkad o mechabit qetanna have pagum, ulekattechilla tzarik lehizzaher apillu bechabit gedola, veyesh omerim gam bemayim pegumim pesulim limzog bahem kos shel birkat hammazon, vetzarik lehizzaher bazeh:

clarification.explanation: The cup must not be defective: if one drank from it, it becomes defective, even if drunk from a jug or small barrel — one should be careful about this even ab initio with a large barrel. Some say that even defective water is unfit to be mixed into the cup of Birkat HaMazon, and one must be careful about this.
takeaways: The cup becomes defective through drinking from it (or from a jug/small barrel)
Some say even defective water is unfit to mix in

paragraphs: Kesheyyaggia lebirkat haaretz beomero uberakta et betebat et yemaggenu bemayim sheenam pegumim, vekatab bechesed laalapim deim hayyayin chazaq shetztzarik harbeh mayim vetzarik name sheyyihyeh hakkos male, lekak yimzegennu qodem birkat hammazon kede sheyyihyeh male veaach"k bebirkat haaretz yosip lemazego bimat mayim ayyen sham, venireh li deyesh lepaqpeq bazeh deha ikka disbira lehu shetztzarik lihyot bitchillat habberaka chay sheeno mazug vezo hassebara niret iqqar, deha beraaya mehemena naqet lah bistama velishar sebarot naqet lehu beshem yesh omerim veim yimzegennu qodem beraka nimtza chaser chay lassebara hannizkeret, al ken "p shetztzarik mayim harbeh umukrach sheyyihyeh chaser chay lassebara hannizkeret, al ken "p shetztzarik mayim harbeh umukrach sheyyihyeh chaser bitchillat habberaka chissuran hannikkar laayin let lan bah meachar shebbebirkat haaretz mozego venaasa male, mihu nireh li al kol panim tzarik sheyyihyeh bo bitchillat habberaka shiur rebiit:

clarification.explanation: When reaching Birkat Ha'aretz, at the word "et," he mixes the cup with water that is not defective. Chesed LaAlafim writes that if the wine is strong and requires much water, and the cup must be full, he should mix it a bit before Birkat HaMazon so it will be full, and add a little more water at Birkat Ha'aretz. But Rabbeinu questions this, since according to those who hold the cup should be "chai" (undiluted) at the start of the berachah (which appears to be the primary view), if he mixes it beforehand it will lack this condition; therefore, even though much water is needed and it will be visibly lacking at the start of the berachah, there is no problem, since it becomes full at Birkat Ha'aretz. Nevertheless, it must contain at least a revi'it at the start of the berachah.
takeaways: One mixes water into the cup at Birkat Ha'aretz, at the word "et," with water that is not defective
It is preferable to leave it "chai" (at least a revi'it) at the start and fill it at Birkat Ha'aretz

paragraphs: Kesheyyimzog hakkos bebirkat haaretz yistakkel bammayim hahem asher yittenem bakkos ukemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l beshaar taame hammitzot parashat eqeb, umeboar sham sheyyekavven hammozeg mayim mispar tishim keminyan tisha yvdy"n shebbearba hvyv"t shel "b s"g m"h b"n yeuyyan sham, veyizzaher gam ken kesheyyimzog lo yattip me hammezig baqqillucha echad, ella yapsiq haqqillucha paam ushettayim kede shettihyeh hammeziga bishlosha peamim zeh achar zeh, ken katebu beshem maabar yabboq za"l vekatabti bsh"q mqbtzyl taam lah bs"d:

clarification.explanation: When mixing the cup at Birkat Ha'aretz, one should look at the water he pours into the cup, and (per the Ari) have intention that the water number ninety, corresponding to the nine yuds within the four Names of Havayah (Ayin-Bet, Samech-Gimmel, Mem-Heh, Bet-Nun). One should also be careful, when mixing, not to pour the water in a single stream, but pause once or twice, so the mixing is done in three separate pourings, one after another.
takeaways: One looks at the water while mixing and has the Ari's intention
One pours the mixing water in three separate streams, not a single stream

paragraphs: Kos shel birkat hammazon veken shel qiddush tzarik sheyyihyeh shalem bispatayv veken babbasis shello shello yihyeh bo pegima vechesron kelal ubishat haddechaq muttar, veyesh mi shepposel apillu bishat haddechaq, vehassedeq apillu belo chissaron posel vekannizkar bechesed laalapim ot d':

clarification.explanation: The cup of Birkat HaMazon, and likewise of Kiddush, must be whole in its rim and in its base, with no defect or deficiency at all; in a time of pressing need it is permitted to use a defective one. Some disqualify it even in a time of pressing need. And a crack — even without any deficiency — disqualifies it (Chesed LaAlafim).
takeaways: The cup for Birkat HaMazon/Kiddush must be whole in rim and base, without defect; in pressing need it is permitted (though some disqualify even then).
A crack disqualifies even without any deficiency.

paragraphs: Mi shennotenin lo kos shel birkat hammazon veeno mebarek meqatztzerin yamayv, mihu haiddana shennahagu bekol teputzot yisrael shekkol echad yebarek birkat hammazon leatzmo veeno yotze yede chobato bibraka shemmebarek baal hakkos - en bazeh chashash hannizkar, deha kol echad mebarek beatzmo umimmela kol echad veechad yebarek gam ken lebaal habbayit veyitqayyem bo vaabarekah mebarekka ubatel taam shel meqatztzerin ak vadday tzarik lirdop achar mitzva zo gam bazzeman hazzeh ki yeqara hi meod, veen notenin kos shel beraka ella letob ayin shehu sone betza veoseh chesed bemamono, shenneemar (mishle kb, t): "tob ayin hu yeborak" al tiqre "yeborak" ella "yebarek" (sota lch:)

clarification.explanation: One who is given the cup of Birkat HaMazon and does not recite the berachah has his days shortened. But nowadays, when the custom throughout all the communities of Israel is that each person recites Birkat HaMazon for himself and does not fulfill his obligation through the berachah of the one holding the cup, this concern does not apply, since each one blesses for himself and also blesses the host, fulfilling "and I will bless those who bless you." Nevertheless, one must certainly still pursue this precious mitzvah even nowadays. And the cup of blessing is given only to one who is "generous of eye" (tov ayin), who hates unjust gain and does kindness with his money, as it is said, "He who is generous of eye shall be blessed," and the Sages expounded: do not read "yevorach" but "yevarech" (he shall bless).
takeaways: Nowadays, since each person recites the berachah for himself, there is no concern of "shortened days"
The cup of blessing is given to one who is "generous of eye" and does kindness with his money
